issues.legal_issue: A defendant may not introduce a counterclaim by amending a written statement when the counterclaim’s cause of action arose after the defendant had delivered the defence.
material_facts: The defendant delivered a written statement in the suit.
The defendant later sought leave to amend the written statement to add a counterclaim for a declaration of ownership and recovery of possession.
The counterclaim stated that the plaintiffs had trespassed on and encroached upon the land in the summer of 1998, after the written statement had been delivered.
issues.conclusion: The application to add the counterclaim was not maintainable, and the courts below were wrong to allow it.
issues.legal_principle: Order VIII Rule 6A of the Code of Civil Procedure permits a counterclaim based on a cause of action accruing before or after institution of the suit only if it arises before the defendant delivers the defence or before the time allowed to deliver it expires. The general ability to amend pleadings under Order VI Rule 17, or to file additional pleadings under Order VIII Rule 9, cannot override that restriction. The Court relied on Mahendra Kumar v. State of Madhya Pradesh, Shanti Rani Das Dewanjee v. Dinesh Chandra Day and Gurbachan Singh v. Bhag Singh on the timing restriction, and Ramesh Chand v. Anil Panjwani on discouraging belated counterclaims; it held that Baldev Singh v. Manohar Singh did not authorize a counterclaim contrary to the restriction and distinguished Sri Ryaz Ahmed on its facts.

predicates.defendant_seeks_counterclaim_in_existing: A defendant in an existing suit seeks to add a counterclaim against the plaintiff.
predicates.defence_already_delivered: The defendant has already delivered the defence in the suit.
predicates.counterclaim_cause_arose_after_defence: The events said to give rise to the counterclaim occurred after the defendant delivered the defence.

issues.definition: When a defendant seeks a counterclaim in an existing suit after delivering the defence, and the counterclaim arises from later events, the counterclaim must not be allowed.

issues.legal_issue: A court may not avoid the statutory timing restriction on a counterclaim by treating a counterclaim that breaches it as a plaint in a cross-suit.
material_facts: The defendant sought to add a counterclaim after delivering the written statement, based in part on alleged trespass occurring afterward.
The counterclaim sought a declaration of ownership and recovery of possession.
The Court considered whether a counterclaim could instead be treated as a plaint in a cross-suit, noting that the counterclaim procedure had a statutory timing restriction.
issues.conclusion: The statutory restriction prevents the court from treating a counterclaim that breaches the restriction as a plaint in a cross-suit in order to grant the requested relief.
issues.legal_principle: In Laxmidas Dayabhai Kabrawala v. Nanabhai Chunilal Kabrawala, the Court recognized that a counterclaim could be treated as a plaint in a cross-suit where no legal bar prevented that course. The Court held that the later insertion of Order VIII Rule 6A of the Code of Civil Procedure imposed a statutory embargo on a counterclaim filed outside its permitted time, and that the court could not exercise its jurisdiction to bypass that embargo.
